headline: macOS 27.3 could change how you grant AI agents Full Disk Access
summary: Apple is tightening privacy controls in a future macOS update, responding to AI agents requesting broad permissions.
details: Apple is set to introduce significant privacy enhancements in an upcoming macOS update, specifically targeting how AI agents access user data.
The move comes in response to concerns about AI tools requesting extensive permissions, including Full Disk Access, which could pose security risks.
The update will likely implement more granular controls, requiring explicit user consent for specific data access requests from AI applications.
This change aims to balance the growing capabilities of AI with the fundamental need for user privacy and data security on macOS.

topic: diamond foundry creates world's first 200mm single-crystal diamond wafer
headline_marked: Diamond Foundry creates [[world's first 200mm single-crystal diamond wafer]]
headline: Diamond Foundry creates world's first 200mm single-crystal diamond wafer
summary: This breakthrough in lab-grown diamond technology promises superior cooling for AI chips, with 300mm wafers targeted by 2030.
details: Diamond Foundry has announced the creation of the world's first 200mm single-crystal diamond (SCD) wafer, a significant advancement for semiconductor cooling. This wafer size is standard in older semiconductor fabrication processes, marking a new era for SCDs.

Diamonds boast exceptional thermal conductivity, estimated to be at least five times greater than copper. This property makes SCDs ideal for managing the intense heat generated by increasingly powerful AI chips, helping to prevent hotspots and improve performance.

Unlike polycrystalline diamonds, Diamond Foundry's SCDs are manufactured as high-quality single crystals. This structure allows for extreme thermal conductivity while maintaining electrical insulation, a crucial combination for advanced cooling solutions.

The company is already looking ahead, with plans to produce 300mm SCD wafers before 2030, matching the size used in leading-edge semiconductor processes. While the current sample requires further polishing for chipmaker use, this milestone represents decades of research and development.

Diamond Foundry CEO Martin Roscheisen highlighted the perseverance of his team, stating, "This is one of those milestones that once seemed almost impossible." He credited "countless experiments, failures, inventions, rebuilt machines, and insights over more than a decade" for the achievement.

Other companies are also exploring lab-grown diamonds for semiconductor cooling. Akash Systems received CHIPS Act funding for GaN fused with synthetic diamond, and De Beers Group is developing a copper-plated diamond composite. Even companies like Frore Systems are investigating diamond-infused cooling solutions for high-performance GPUs.
